title: Global health progress is moving in the right direction but remains off track, with pandemic scars and weak mortality information limiting public capacity to see and respond
source_unit: World Health Organization, World health statistics 2026: monitoring health for the SDGs
geography: WHO Member States, regions, and global health indicators associated with the Sustainable Development Goals

denominator.unit: health-related SDG indicators with a numeric SDG or other global target

indicators_on_track.unit: health-related indicators judged on track globally for their 2030 target

direction_of_change.value: many indicators continue to improve, including universal health coverage, key infectious diseases, safe water, sanitation, hygiene, and clean cooking

tobacco_alcohol.value: tobacco use and alcohol consumption have declined since 2010 but not fast enough to fully meet global targets

observations.method: WHO annual compilation of the latest available health and health-related indicators and progress toward health-related SDG targets.
observations.uncertainty: The global assessment aggregates indicators with different reference years, coverage, definitions, and target structures; no single score represents population health or service quality.
observations.subgroup: Populations, health systems, governments, and communities across WHO regions and income settings.
observations.counterinterpretation: A zero-indicator on-track assessment does not mean every health outcome is worsening; it identifies insufficient aggregate pace relative to 2030 ambitions.

observations.period: 2020-2023; global excess mortality associated with the COVID-19 pandemic

global_excess_deaths.unit: estimated excess deaths globally from 2020 through 2023

reported_covid_deaths.unit: reported COVID-19 deaths used for comparison

observations.method: WHO modelled excess mortality compares all-cause deaths with expected historical mortality and captures direct and indirect pandemic effects.
observations.uncertainty: Excess mortality is modelled where registration is incomplete and is not a clinical classification of each death or a causal decomposition of all indirect effects.
observations.subgroup: Populations affected by infection, care disruption, delayed treatment, reporting gaps, and health-system strain.
observations.counterinterpretation: Declining excess mortality after 2021 indicates recovery from the peak even though cumulative mortality remains far above reported COVID-19 deaths.

observations.period: 2019-2023; life expectancy and healthy life expectancy recovery

denominator.unit: global and WHO-region life-expectancy comparison frame

recovery_pattern.value: overall life expectancy and healthy life expectancy remained slightly below 2019 levels in the latest comparison

female_recovery.value: female life expectancy fully rebounded by 2023

uneven_recovery.value: recovery is uneven across regions, with overlapping pandemic, disaster, and armed-conflict shocks straining systems

observations.method: WHO global health estimates and regional comparison of life expectancy and healthy life expectancy before and after the pandemic period.
observations.uncertainty: Life expectancy and HALE are population averages; they do not measure disability, care access, lived well-being, or the distribution of recovery within a country.
observations.subgroup: Women and men, WHO regions, lower-income and higher-income populations, and communities exposed to overlapping shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Long-run gains in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment remain substantial; a modest aggregate shortfall from 2019 does not erase those gains.

deaths_reported_with_cause.unit: deaths reported to WHO with cause-of-death information

detailed_icd_coded_deaths.unit: deaths reported with detailed three- or four-digit ICD coding

meaningful_cause_information.unit: deaths with meaningful cause-of-death information after ill-defined or unspecified causes are accounted for

information_share.unit: approximate share of estimated global deaths with meaningful cause-of-death information

institutional_role.value: civil registration and vital statistics support legal identity, emergency detection, inequality measurement, resource allocation, and health planning

observations.method: WHO comparison of estimated global deaths with deaths reported through civil registration and vital-statistics systems and medically certified, ICD-coded causes.
observations.uncertainty: The figures reflect reporting and coding coverage as well as mortality; they do not identify which populations are missing from registration or establish why reporting capacity differs.
observations.subgroup: Countries with incomplete civil registration, families needing legal identity, public-health authorities, and communities whose mortality patterns are undercounted.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved registration may initially reveal more deaths or causes without indicating a worsening health situation; visibility is a prerequisite for better response, not evidence of response by itself.

related_sources.claim: Official WHO publication page for World health statistics 2026 and its publication metadata.
WHO annual World Health Statistics index with 2026 tables and visual-summary links.

boundary: This record adds an aggregate health-progress, pandemic-mortality, life-expectancy-recovery, and mortality-information route. It uses WHO indicators, modelled estimates, and health-system reporting synthesis, not respondent-level medical histories, patient records, individual treatment effects, household health diaries, or proof that better measurement automatically improves care.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official WHO World health statistics 2026 publication page, WHO annual-report index, and visual summary reviewed for SDG progress, excess mortality, life-expectancy recovery, and civil-registration findings.
